passages.text: Now I am old, elderly and senior. I’m advanced in years and have reached the final stage of life. I’m currently eighty years old. Just as a decrepit old cart is kept going by a rope, in the same way, the Realized One’s body is kept going as if by a rope.
passages.note: Ageing; a frail body near the end of life

passages.text: So Ānanda, live as your own island, your own refuge, with no other refuge. Let the teaching be your island and your refuge, with no other refuge.
passages.note: Self-reliance when a guide or support is leaving

passages.text: “Sāriputta, someone whose mind is free is a great man, I say. If their mind is not free, I say they’re not a great man.
passages.note: True greatness is inner freedom, not status

passages.text: But Venerable Sāriputta was my adviser and counselor. He educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired me. He never tired of teaching the Dhamma, and he supported his spiritual companions.
passages.note: Grieving a mentor; remembering what they gave

passages.text: “Ānanda, did I not prepare for this when I explained that we must be parted and separated from all we hold dear and beloved? How could it possibly be so that what is born, created, conditioned, and liable to wear out should not wear out? That is not possible.
passages.note: Grief and loss; all we love must part from us
